relationships.subject: FABP5
relationships.evidence_quote: Our present results demonstrate that FABP5 mediates AEA transport in DRGs as its deletion elevates AEA levels

relationships.subject: FABP5 deletion in nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, FABP5 deletion suppresses inflammation- and nerve growth factor-mediated TRPV1 sensitization via CB1, an effect mediated by calcineurin.

relationships.subject: FABP5 deletion in nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP release was suppressed in both FABP5 KO and cKO mice following carrageenan challenge

relationships.subject: NGF
relationships.evidence_quote: Carrageenan-evoked hyperalgesia is dependent upon nerve growth factor (NGF) release, which plays an obligate role in TRPV1 sensitization

relationships.subject: PF3845
relationships.evidence_quote: application of the selective FAAH inhibitor PF3845 failed to blunt NGF-mediated TRPV1 sensitization despite elevating AEA levels in DRGs

relationships.subject: anandamide
relationships.evidence_quote: AEA is also a TRPV1 agonist and inflammatory mediators such as prostaglandin E2 increase its efficacy and potency at TRPV1

key_findings: FABP5 deletion in TRPV1+ nociceptors elevates AEA, PEA and OEA and produces CB1- and PPARα-mediated antinociception
FABP5 deletion blunts NGF-mediated TRPV1 sensitization via CB1 and calcineurin, whereas FAAH inhibition does not
